newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia stock agency warns against manipulation.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia stock agency warns against manipulation.

text.p: The head of Indonesia's Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam) warned on Friday against attempts to manipulate stock prices.

"Don't try to manipulate prices. We are watching closely. We will intervene in the market if necessary," I Gede Putu Ary Suta told reporters while attending a two-day conference on capital flows on the tropical island of Bali.
Suta was responding to questions on recent heavy fluctuations in stock prices, especially in second- and third-liner stocks on the Jakarta Stock Exchange (JSE).
"It's the duty of the JSE to act if prices are fluctuating. We will only intervene if the JSE is not doing its job," he said.
Suta said the recent swings in the price of Astra International shares had not violated capital market laws.

Astra, the country's largest automobile manufacturer, gained sharply last week on reported comments by timber tycoon Muhamad (Bob) Hasan that the Nusamba group he controls is interested in buying into the company.
It slipped this week when a newspaper quoted Hasan as saying Nusamba did not plan a general offer but would pick up shares at market prices.
Suta said Hasan had not violated regulations because he was not on the board of Astra.
